headline: High-risk write and action conflicts: OpenHands can modify shared runtime state while MinerU can feed unverified document outputs into downstream agent loops.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can expose parsed document text through MCP/API surfaces, and OpenHands can consume MCP-backed inputs in an agent loop. A shared filesystem is not required, but if MinerU outputs attacker-controlled document content into OpenHands without provenance checks, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pairwise bridge is documented only at the profile level, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into OpenHands as prompt text or task context
IF the MCP channel lacks provenance tagging or content sanitization
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all MinerU outputs before handoff
Strip imperative phrases from extracted text before passing to OpenHands
Require OpenHands to treat MinerU output as untrusted data by default
Use a separate MCP server per agent
requires-engineering: implement content-signature checks across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, while OpenHands reads and writes files in its runtime sandbox and can use mounted volumes. If sensitive documents are mounted into both or copied between them, OpenHands may expose that content through its broader runtime and networked model-provider path. The shared workspace path is plausible but not proven, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are mounted into both runtimes
IF OpenHands forwards file contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep MinerU inputs in a separate read-only directory
Do not mount the same workspace into OpenHands
Redact secrets before copying outputs between agents
Disable model-provider access for sensitive runs
requires-engineering: add per-file data-class routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification inside its runtime, while MinerU can also use MCP and process local files. If both are pointed at the same mounted volume or repo, concurrent writes and state changes can collide and corrupt outputs or git state. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking mechanism, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory or repository
IF OpenHands performs git operations while MinerU writes extracted artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent
Freeze git operations while MinerU runs
Use read-only mounts for MinerU inputs
Serialize access with a simple file lock
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing agent that can emit extracted text, tables, and OCR results, and OpenHands is an action-capable coding agent with shell, browser, and git authority. If OpenHands treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or runtime actions. The pathway exists in default agent-loop usage, but verification can mitigate it.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses MinerU output as task truth without independent checks
IF extracted OCR or table data drives code edits or browser actions
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Cross-check key fields against the source document
Ask OpenHands to cite the exact extracted spans it used
Limit MinerU output to summaries for high-stakes tasks
requires-engineering: add validation against source-document hashes

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while OpenHands runs in a Docker runtime and can send data to a user-configured model provider. A compliance mismatch is possible if regulated documents are processed by OpenHands after MinerU extraction, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict. Because only OpenHands has an explicit third-party transmission path, it is the main cited agent.
conditions: IF regulated data extracted by MinerU is then sent from OpenHands to a non-approved model provider
IF retention or residency rules apply to the mounted runtime files
mitigations: Keep regulated documents inside MinerU only
Use an approved model provider for OpenHands
Disable external API calls for regulated runs
Document retention settings for the runtime
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
